analysis.summary: Borana Weaves Limited reported strong financial growth for the quarter and year ended March 31, 2026, driven by scaling operations in unbleached synthetic greige fabric and PTY yarn. Management highlighted strategic initiatives including renewable energy integration through a hybrid solar-wind project, upcoming capacity expansions aimed at doubling production capacity over the next 24 months, and expanding into technical and RPU-coated fabrics. The company maintained robust profitability, with annual revenue increasing to ₹388.59 crores and PAT rising to ₹64.61 crores. Borana Weaves Limited reported strong operational and financial performance for Q3 FY26, driven by higher volumes, improved capacity utilization, and robust order books. Management highlighted ongoing capacity expansions, including the addition of high-speed water jet looms and a strategic transition towards renewable energy to optimize power costs.

capex_expansion.quote: And the cost of this project will be around INR35 crores.

margins_costs.claim: Gross profit for FY26 was reported at ₹160.75 crores with a gross profit margin of 41.37%.
EBITDA for FY26 stood at ₹91.52 crores representing an EBITDA margin of 23.55%.
EBITDA for Q3 FY26 stood at 27.09 crores with a margin of 24.32%.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR27.09 crores, registered a strong 51% Y-on-Y growth with a margin of 24.32%.

margins_costs.claim: Nine-month EBITDA rose by 44% year-on-year to 65.9 crores with a margin of 22.89%.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA rose by 44% Y-on-Y to INR65.9 crores, broadly in line with a revenue growth reflecting healthy operating leverage with a margin of 22.89%.

margins_costs.claim: Strong floor efficiency supported by a low operating cost structure across power, fuel, and labor continues to support margins.
margins_costs.quote: Strong floor efficiency supported by relatively low operating cost structure across the power, fuel and labor continuously to support the margins.

margins_costs.claim: Operating leverage was clearly visible, with EBITDA rising 51 percent year-on-year to Rs 27.1 crore and margins expanding to 24.3 percent.
margins_costs.quote: Operating leverage was clearly visible, with EBITDA rising 51% YoY to ₹27.1 crore and margins expanding to 24.3%.

margins_costs.claim: Capacity expansion and higher renewable energy usage are expected to improve operating margins.
margins_costs.quote: Capacity expansion and higher renewable energy usage are expected to improve operating margins
